subject.title: fix: workflow sanity audit passes on main

question: Is the fallback GitHub App installation intentionally approved to mint a token with `contents: read`, and can maintainers provide or authorize a controlled fallback-path validation?
rationale: The repository configuration and App-installation approval are outside this PR’s source diff; without that intent, the fallback path can either fail token minting or unnecessarily broaden an App permission boundary.

options.title: Confirm and prove fallback access
options.body: Confirm the fallback installation has approved read-only Contents access and attach redacted logs from a controlled primary-token failure that completes label configuration loading and labeling.

options.title: Keep fallback least-privilege
options.body: If the fallback App should not receive Contents access, redesign the configuration-read path so fallback labeling does not require that permission.

options.title: Pause the change
options.body: Leave the existing fallback contract unchanged until the App-installation permission boundary has an owner decision and reproducible proof.

recommendation.title: Confirm and prove fallback access
recommendation.body: Confirm the fallback installation has approved read-only Contents access and attach redacted logs from a controlled primary-token failure that completes label configuration loading and labeling.

likelyOwner.reason: This requires an upstream decision about the organization-managed fallback GitHub App installation, not only a source-level patch review.
